market.headline: Stocks fell for a third day on Monday, led by chips. Nvidia reports tonight after the close.
points: Chips: The Nasdaq dropped 2.5% and the S&P 500 fell 1.9% on Monday. Nvidia lost 4%, AMD almost 6% and TSMC about 6%. A new US rule makes it harder to rent out advanced chips to Chinese firms through data centres in other countries, and adds licences for some Southeast Asia sales.

Rates: The 10-year US bond yield is about 5.1%, well above its early November low of 4.8%. Last week's inflation report was hotter than expected, so traders lean toward a Fed rate hike in December. Higher rates usually weigh on pricey growth stocks and on home spending.
Politics: Trump and Elon Musk are in China this week around the APEC meetings. After the Democrats' big midterm wins, some investors worry about new limits on AI data centres.

Events: US retail sales come out this morning and Nvidia reports around 4:20 pm Eastern. Wednesday has the Fed's meeting notes and Anthropic's IPO pricing, with trading starting Thursday. P&G holds an investor day Thursday.
market.plan: Stay patient. The biggest event of the week lands tonight, so let Nvidia's results and Wednesday's reaction pass before buying any tech. If you want to start something now, keep it small and pick the calm, non-tech names.

stocks.sum: The simple, certified way to own about 220 halal US companies at once.
why: Down about 7% from its high as of Friday, and the market fell again Monday, so you are not buying at the top.
One purchase spreads your money over many companies, so one bad stock hurts less.
Certified halal, so there is no screening homework.
risk: Nvidia is about 10% of the fund and Apple about 14%, so tonight's Nvidia results will move it.
I could not confirm Monday's close. The price shown is Friday's, and with the market down about 2% Monday it is likely a bit lower now.
stocks.todo: Still a fine first purchase, but split it. Buy a small first piece now and the rest after Nvidia reports.

stocks.sum: A calm, Canadian-dollar halal fund. No currency fee when you buy it.
why: Trades in Canadian dollars, so you skip the 1.5% US currency fee each way.
Holds steady companies around the world and moves much less than tech.
Certified halal.
risk: Slow mover. Good for safety, weak for quick gains.
I found a fresh Nov 13 close of $37.46, but not a reliable 52-week range, so the range is hidden for now. Check the live price in Wealthsimple.
stocks.todo: A sensible place for money you can't afford to see swing, like a down payment. Check the live price first.

stocks.n: SP Funds Dow Jones Global Sukuk ETF
stocks.sum: A halal income fund that pays monthly, about 4.9% a year. Not a growth play.
why: Pays a small amount every month.
Barely moves when stocks drop.
risk: It slid five days in a row to $17.43, right next to its 52-week low of $17.37. Rising interest rates tend to push funds like this lower.
US withholding tax takes 15% of the payouts inside an FHSA.
stocks.todo: Only use it to park cash for income. It will not help a few-month profit goal.

stocks.earnNote: Nvidia, its biggest driver, reports Nov 17
stocks.sum: The chip rebound trade without leverage, spread over 26 chip makers.
why: About 28% below its high as of Friday, so there is real room to recover.
It spreads you across Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, TSMC and others, so you do not have to guess which one wins.
risk: It moves almost twice as much as the market. It slid about 5% more on Monday, but I could not confirm the exact close, so the price shown is Friday's.
Nvidia's results tonight will swing it hard either way, and the new US chip rule adds pressure on the whole group.
stocks.todo: Wait for Nvidia's results. If chips hold up on Wednesday and Thursday, think about one share.

stocks.sum: The AI chip leader, down about a third with no permanent CEO, reporting tonight.
why: About 36% below its high and cheap against its expected profits.
Analysts' average target is far above today's price, though many have been cutting their targets this week.
risk: Earnings land tonight at about 4:20 pm Eastern, the first since Jensen Huang resigned. Big overnight moves are normal for this stock.
The finance chief is filling in as CEO. Reports say Huang's return is not being discussed, and the Treasury Secretary has urged an outside hire.
The new rule on renting chips to Chinese firms abroad could cut into sales. It fell 4% on Monday.
stocks.todo: Do not buy before earnings. Look again Wednesday once the price settles.

stocks.sum: A big winner from custom AI chips, about 30% below its high.
why: Some of the money leaving Nvidia has been moving into Broadcom.
Analysts' average target is well above the price.
risk: It fell about 4% on Monday, its second down day in a row, on the tighter US chip rules.
Its own earnings on Dec 9 are the next big test, and Nvidia's results tonight will move it first.
stocks.todo: Wait until after Nvidia reports. If you buy, plan to be out or smaller before Dec 9.

stocks.sum: Strong business, but the wildest stock on this list.
why: Record quarter on Nov 3 and gaining ground on Nvidia.
risk: It fell almost 9% on Friday and almost 6% more on Monday. It moves two and a half times as much as the market.
Singapore was about 12% of its sales last year, so the new US licence rules for Southeast Asia are a direct risk.
Very expensive against current profits, so bad news hits it hard.
stocks.todo: Skip it for now. A normal stop can't protect you well on a stock that swings this much.

stocks.sum: Makes the chips for nearly every AI company, so it wins whoever leads.
why: About 23% below its high, and it just reported a record month of sales.
It makes chips for nearly every AI company, so it is less tied to who leads Nvidia.
risk: It fell about 6% on Monday and nearly 10% in three days. Taiwan's market had one of its worst days on record.
Taiwan and US-China politics are a standing risk, and Trump is in China this week. The new US chip rule adds more noise.
stocks.todo: Wait for Nvidia's results and the China trip headlines, then consider one share.

stocks.sum: The steady one. It held up through the whole chip selloff.
why: Only about 7% below its high while chip stocks fell much harder. It lost just 1% on Monday.
Moves about the same as the market, so the stop can be tighter.
Its own earnings are already out, so no company surprise is due soon.
risk: One share is about $735 CAD, a big piece of a small account.
Microsoft traced last week's outage to a software bug and rolled it back. A final report is due Nov 20.
It is still a tech stock, so Nvidia's results tonight can pull it around for a day or two.
stocks.todo: A fair buy for one share. Use a limit order a little under the last price, or wait until Wednesday if this week's news makes you uneasy.

stocks.sum: The cheapest big tech name against its profits, about 30% below its high.
why: Its price-to-earnings is near 15, which is low for a big tech company. That means you pay less for each dollar of profit.
Its income comes from ads and cloud, so it depends less on chip spending.
Its own earnings are already out.
risk: It fell 3.5% on Monday after news it will buy about $10 billion of Anthropic shares in the IPO, plus worries about heavy AI spending.
Anthropic starts trading Thursday. A strong or weak debut could move Alphabet too.
It sits only about 5% above its 52-week low. Cheap stocks can get cheaper.
stocks.todo: Hold off a few days. Let Nvidia's results and the Anthropic debut pass, then look at buying one share.

stocks.sum: A safe haven lately, but priced at the top.
why: Investors moved into Apple while chips fell. It slipped only 1% on Monday.
risk: It sits about 2% below its all-time high and already above analysts' average target.
Pricey against profits, so there is little room left for a few-month trade.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Put it on your list for a pullback of 8% or more.

stocks.sum: A story stock. The price runs on headlines more than on profits.
why: About 24% below its high, and it is pushing ahead with its Cybercab robotaxi.
risk: Extremely expensive against its profits.
It swings on headlines. Musk is in China this week, there is talk of a SpaceX merger, and its China sales fell sharply in October.
stocks.todo: Skip for a planned, rule-based trade. Too unpredictable.

stocks.sum: Reasonably priced and about 20% below its high, but the halal status needs your own check.
why: Fair price against profits, and analysts' target is well above today's price.
risk: Halal screeners do not all agree on Meta. Check Zoya or Musaffa first.
Italy's privacy watchdog fined it about 805 million euros, and it is borrowing heavily to pay for AI.
Like all big tech, it will react to Nvidia's results tonight.
stocks.todo: Settle the halal question first. If it passes for you, look again after Nvidia reports.

stocks.sum: The weight-loss drug leader, sitting about 2% below a record high.
why: Not a tech stock, so it spreads your risk.
It barely moves with the market, and it just agreed to buy a small cancer drug company.
risk: Near its high and right at analysts' average target, so the easy gains are behind it.
One share costs about $2,030 CAD.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Too big for one share on a $10,000 account, and no discount.

stocks.sum: A defensive stock that investors ran to during the tech selloff.
why: Very calm. It hardly reacts to market drops.
risk: About 2% below its high and above analysts' average target, so you would be buying after the run.
Ongoing talc lawsuits, and an insider sold shares this week.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Good company, wrong price for a new trade.

why: A discount without tech's wild swings.
Steady product news: a new heart device lead won US approval and it launched a COVID and flu home test in Canada.
A low share price means you can buy several shares and size the trade exactly.
risk: The price shown is Friday's close. I could not confirm Monday's, so check today's price first.
Health stocks can stay out of favour for a long time.
stocks.todo: A good non-tech pick. Confirm the price and the halal status, then buy in one go.

why: People buy its products in any economy, and it just raised its dividend for the 70th year in a row.
risk: Less than 1% below its high as of Friday.
Its investor day is Thursday, Nov 19, which can move the price.
I could not confirm Monday's close, so the price shown is Friday's.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Useful as a safe corner later, not as a profit trade now.

stocks.sum: Beat forecasts this morning and named a new CEO, but the stock slipped before the open.
why: Sales and profit came in a little above forecasts, and it kept its full-year plan near the top of its range.
Fair price against profits, and older US homes need repairs.
risk: Shares were down about 2% before the open, near $339. Fewer shoppers came in, even though each one spent more.
The finance chief, Richard McPhail, takes over as CEO on Nov 23. Leadership changes can bring new plans and surprises.
High interest rates slow home sales and big renovation jobs, and rates are going up.
stocks.todo: Earnings are done, but let the price settle for a few days and watch how it reacts to rates and Nvidia before buying.

why: About 5% below its high and calmer than the market.
It has raised its dividend for decades, which signals a stable business.
Nothing to do with the AI trade, so it spreads your risk.
risk: One share is about $745 CAD.
The gap to analysts' target is small, so expect slow gains.
